criteria.pass_when: Uses a small supported diagram with readable explanation, or an explicit readable text fallback if rendering is unavailable. Shows hit, miss, fill and error paths without implying every request reaches the database.
criteria.evidence: Rendered diagram when available plus semantic edge/direction inspection against flow.txt; source code alone does not prove rendering.

criteria.pass_when: Explains that a database failure affects misses while cache hits can still return; makes no fresh operational claim.
criteria.evidence: Final visible explanation and diagram labels checked against supplied facts.

calibration_pairs.facts: The browser sends a request to the API. The API checks the cache. A hit returns through the API to the browser. A miss reads the database, fills the cache, then returns through the API to the browser. A database error on a miss returns an error through the API; no successful cache fill occurs.
calibration_pairs.good:
Browser → API → cache lookup
Hit: cache → API → browser
Miss: database read → cache fill → API → browser
Read failure: error → API → browser; no successful fill.

A database failure affects misses; cache hits can still return.
calibration_pairs.poor: Browser, API, cache lookup, cache hit, API, browser, cache miss, database read, cache fill, API, browser, read error, API, browser, no successful fill. Database failure affects misses and cache hits can still return.
calibration_pairs.distinction: Both mention the same components; explicit branches and direction make the good version usable. Do not pass a diagram that loses the failure branch.
